description: The adversarial set: every edge case, ambiguity, and interaction the v0.7.0 spec had to settle, each with its EXACT declared outcome — which problem/advisory fires at what severity and location, or that the case builds clean. Cases that cannot live in git (case-only twins, symlinks, nested .git, --clean containment) are generated at runtime by runtime-cases.mjs and share this expectation schema.

harnessContract.run: per case: unify build -s <case>/src -o <tmp>/dist <flags>, wrapped in a hard 30s timeout — the v0.6 engine hung forever on a missing <include>; a hang is a failure, never a wait.
harnessContract.diagnostics: stderr parsed via the stable `FILE:LINE: SEVERITY: ` prefix (line optional). Declared lists are exhaustive when diagnosticsExhaustive=true: one undeclared diagnostic of either severity fails the case. This is the mechanical enforcement of the closed problem/advisory catalogue (conformance spec §14.2/§14.3) and of the content-loss law's flip side — nothing may fire that the spec does not name.
harnessContract.trees: when expectedTree is set, comparison is byte-exact and bidirectional. expectFiles/expectAbsent assert presence/absence relative to the output dir. expectContains maps output files to required substrings; expectNotContains to forbidden ones.
harnessContract.publish: published=false cases pre-seed the output dir with a sentinel tree and assert it byte-untouched after the run (PUB-01), and assert exit matches.
harnessContract.stdout: stdoutContains/stdoutNotContains assert substrings of stdout (the build summary). Used by the runtime-built §4.4 defaulted-source-notice cases, whose entries also carry omitSourceFlag (the harness injects no implicit -s — EXC-11's predicate is the absence of --source) and outputDir (where expectFiles are asserted); diagnostics stay a stderr-only claim.
harnessContract.severityTokens: the parser accepts only 'problem' and 'advisory' as severity tokens; any 'warning'/'error:' line fails the case (DIA-01).

retired-vocab-in-excluded.note: R1 promoted to spec text (2026-08-12): conformance §6.3 now says outright that 'anywhere in any source file' includes excluded files — build material is scanned; only the never-shipped list escapes.

missing-include.note: The v0.6 engine looped forever on this input. The 30s harness timeout makes a hang a hard failure. The 'casing' assertion pins the mandatory fix line for path-shaped problems (DIA-07).

include-cycle.note: Attribution at the outermost include site — R3, promoted to contract in conformance §14.1 (2026-08-12).

include-depth-10.note: Fencepost: a chain of exactly 10 nested expansions builds clean; 11 fails (next case). R2 promoted to spec text (2026-08-12): conformance §5.1 now states the cap is inclusive — the stack holds ten files, the include pushing an eleventh is the problem.

include-with-content.note: The include target exists; exactly one problem fires — the content one. Includes are verbatim, never components.

layout-declares-layout.note: C7 / FIX-14: a layout that declares data-layout is P15 — layout chaining is not supported in v0.7.0 and is never a silent no-op. The declared target (_base.html) exists, so the only diagnostic is P15 itself.

content-nowhere.note: The exact failure v0.6 shipped silently (content deleted, exit 0, success banner). Here it must block publish, name the layout, and leave the sentinel output untouched.

slot-in-template.note: C9: the template's slot is not unify's — the fill gets advisory 2, the template ships byte-identical, the fill's content stays in the page flow.

slot-attr-edge.note: slot= on a nested element is the author's web-component markup: never touched, never reported, ships with the attribute intact. slot="" is not a fill. Zero diagnostics is the assertion.

nested-main-in-div.note: R4 promoted to spec text (2026-08-12): conformance §7.2 now says the first <main> unwraps at any depth — the main inside the div unwraps; the div survives.

main-in-main.note: Unwrap happens exactly once — now explicit in conformance §7.2 (R4): the outer main's tags are deleted, the inner main survives into the output (the author's own nesting, preserved).

empty-md.note: A zero-byte .md page builds: .html swap happens, no h1 means no page title, the layout's title stands alone (separator included — that is the specified behavior), the layout main keeps its children.

collision-md-html.note: One problem naming both sources; attribution at the path-ordered first source — R3, promoted to contract in conformance §14.1. No last-write-wins: nothing publishes.

collision-pretty-landing-noflag.note: The same tree is legal without --pretty-urls: the collision exists only under the move.

underscore-guard.note: Replacing the default exclude set cannot silently publish working files: the guard names each _-page/_-dir path and the fixing --exclude line.

netlify-headers.note: The conformance §4.2 recipe verbatim: _headers/_redirects ship (non-page files, guard passes them), _layout.html/_includes stay excluded and still drive composition. The A14 side of the coin: with the deployment files shipping, the deployment-file advisory must stay silent — an advisory that fires on a correct site is a bug, and diagnosticsExhaustive asserts the silence.

deploy-file-excluded.note: Default excludes hold back root-level _headers/_redirects/_routes.json — known deployment files (conformance §4.2), so each draws advisory A14 naming the file and the --exclude line that ships it. The advisory is the whole mechanism: the files stay excluded (expected tree is index.html alone), the build publishes, exit 0. blog/_headers draws nothing — recognition is by name at the source root only.

stranded-underscore-asset.note: The spec's own §11.1 trap: the include's relative logo resolves to /_includes/logo.png, which the default exclude keeps out of the output — the reference check must fail loudly. Attribution at the provenance file — R3, promoted to contract in conformance §14.1.

handwritten-pretty-url.note: Write href to the real file, never a hand-written pretty URL: /about/ resolves to /about/index.html, which no build without --pretty-urls emits.

style-url-not-rewritten.note: url() inside <style> and style= is never rewritten (byte-equality proves it) while BOTH are reference-checked — B5 closed (2026-08-12): §12 now covers style-attribute url() too; dot.png exists, so this side builds clean. The firing twin is style-attr-url-broken.

style-attr-url-broken.note: B5's firing side: a url() in a style ATTRIBUTE pointing at nothing is a broken reference like any other — rewriting stays exempt (§11.1), checking does not (§12). The v0.6-shaped alternative was shipping the 404 silently.

dollar-patterns.note: $&, $1, $', $`, $$ inside fragments and fills must survive byte-for-byte. This is a direct regression trap for String.prototype.replace-based splicing.

working-format.note: Advisories never change what is published: the files still ship.

working-format-strict.note: Under --strict the same advisories flip the exit code and block publish — a stray .psd can never cost a publish silently.

frontmatter-junk-keys.note: draft:true publishes; date/permalink/slug/tags are inert plain metas; permalink does NOT move the output (dist/post.html). B6 closed (2026-08-12): §10.2 value serialization pinned exact — plain scalars as source text ('true', '2026-01-01', '0.50' keeps its zero), quoted scalars unquoted ('Colons: kept…'), empty value → content="". The no-text-form firing twin is frontmatter-deep-nest (P17).

frontmatter-deep-nest.note: P17: a mapping nested below a block (og: → image: → url:) has no text form — frontmatter flattens exactly one level, and both inventing a serialization and dropping the value would be silent lies. Located at the key whose value nests (line 4). The list-item-that-is-a-mapping branch is the same problem.

charset-page-only.note: Layout declares no charset: the page's is kept and moved to the head's first position on its own line with the first-content-line indentation — byte-exact.

md-include-element.note:
B2 resolved (2026-08-12): conversion first, includes resolve on the converted HTML, and a line-initial is a block (the §10.1 type-6 extension). Exact tree pins all three placements: line-initial paired form splices as a clean block (never

-wrapped), an include inside a sentence splices inline within the paragraph, and a code-fenced include is escaped text that resolution never touches. The page is layout-less, so the §10.7 shell wraps it (MD-20).

srcset-poster-rewrite.note: srcset URLs rewritten per candidate with descriptors untouched; poster rewritten; both from layout provenance.

base-url-subpath.note: B3's exact trap, pinned fixed (2026-08-12): a full base URL whose path is not / must absolutize og:/twitter:/canonical as origin + path prefix — og:image /assets/hero.jpg emits https://example.com/repo/assets/hero.jpg, never https://example.com/assets/hero.jpg. href/src get the path part only; the absolute og:url is untouched (URL-12); the reference check must strip the full base to keep the absolutized values checkable (REF-02).

no-layout-anywhere.note: Selection step 5: no layout found anywhere — the page is emitted from its own text, byte-identical.

layout-none-md.note: B4 resolved (2026-08-12): a layout-less .md page emits inside the §10.7 minimal shell — this tree is the spec's own §10.7 fixture verbatim. Exact assertions: charset first, title from the first h1, metas in source order, lang on <html>, class on <body>, converted body in <body>; the present _layout.html did not apply (bidirectional exactness proves its title never leaked in) and is not emitted.

stray-header-footer.note: Advisory, not silent replacement (the v0.6 landmark matcher would have swallowed these): both ship in place per the content-loss law.

slot-in-filled-fallback.note: B1 resolved by spec amendment (2026-08-12): slots do not nest. A <slot> inside another slot's fallback is P16, located at the layout, so the fill-stranding case the old outermost-first rule created can no longer arise. The page is plain default content; the single problem is exhaustive.

two-problems-one-pass.note: Best-effort composition: both problems in one run, ordered by path — authors never fix errors one build at a time.

fragment-links-ok.note: #fragment targets are never validated against ids; fragment-only links are skipped by rewriting entirely.

frontmatter-invalid-yaml.note: P18: the frontmatter does not parse as YAML (an unterminated flow sequence). Distinct from P17, which is about a value's shape in frontmatter that parsed fine — the fix here is repairing syntax, not flattening a structure. Before P18 existed the spec's closed problem list had no ID for a parse failure at all, so an implementation had to either crash or borrow P17.

frontmatter-flat-key-nest.note: P17 via the flat spelling: og:image: with a block under it is the same defect as og: -> image: -> url:, because both name the key og:image and it already carries its prefix. Pins that P17 eligibility is decided by the key's NAME, not by counting recursion levels — a depth-counting implementation would accept this one and reject its block-spelled twin, breaking the spelling equivalence §10.2 guarantees.
